title: Bai Garden Grafting Chronicle
note: SUT-facing prompt stream. Read segments in order; no labels are provided by design.

segments.prompt: At dusk, Qiao Bai（Fruit-tree grafting master Qiao Bai around fifty, straw hat and green rubber boots, grafting-knife sheath at the waist, resin stains on both hands） enters the nursery shed（Nursery shed: an open shed ringed by bamboo fence; wax seals and ties on the table; air of grass and resin） and first wipes the grafting knife（A short-handled grafting knife, blade like a mirror, wood handle carved Bai, cowhide sheath） at his waist.
A row of five bamboo tags（A row of five bamboo tags stuck in the rootstock berm, written with variety and date） sticks in the rootstock berm; Qiao Bai checks each handwritten date.
Two wind chimes（Two wind chimes hung under the shed eaves, chiming lightly when the wind rises） hang under the shed eaves; Qiao Bai reaches to make them chime softly.
Qiao Bai circles the workbench checking whether the wax seals have set.
From the shed Qiao Bai looks toward the darkening green seedlings of the rootstock bed.
The grafting-knife blade mirrors lamp light; Qiao Bai gently tests the edge.
Qiao Bai sits on a bamboo chair in the shed corner for a brief rest.
Qiao Bai opens the phenology notebook（An oilcloth-cover phenology notebook logging budbreak, bloom, and graft survival rates）—this oilcloth phenology book—and marks plump bud-eye spots bed by bed.
Qiao Bai draws rootstock budbreak progress in green line and marks bud-graft survival with red dots.
Qiao Bai closes the phenology book and returns it to the workbench wood box of wax seals and ties.
The grafting knife clicks into its sheath; Qiao Bai nods.
Qiao Bai wipes mud flecks from the cover with a dry cloth and tucks in a budded scion as a specimen.

At the morning rootstock bed（Rootstock bed: neat rows of apple rootstock seedlings; bamboo tags on the berms; soil moist）, Qiao Bai greets young Aya（Apprentice Aya of fourteen or fifteen, indigo headscarf and yellow vest, bright stubborn eyes） arriving in the orchard tractor（A red orchard tractor with rootstock seedlings in the bed, white Bai Garden letters sprayed on the door）.
Aya jumps down from the tractor and rights the rootstock seedlings in the bed.
Qiao Bai points to the three Fuji scion bundles（Three bundles of Fuji scions wrapped in wet hemp cloth in the shed shade, bud eyes plump） in the shed shade and teaches Aya to read plump bud eyes.
Aya crouches on the berm, curiously touching the writing on the bamboo tags.
Qiao Bai explains bud-graft angle; Aya nods carefully.
Aya glances back at the red orchard tractor, eyes full of longing.
Qiao Bai has Aya first practice wrapping the graft union tight with ties.

In the noisy fruit market（Fruit market: open-air market at the town mouth; baskets of apples and pears; scale beams swinging; noisy crowd）, Asui（Young Asui whose face closely resembles Aya's, cream silk scarf and the same yellow vest, flamboyant look） in a cream silk scarf looks up from behind apple baskets.
Asui picks sample fruit at the scale; the scarf sways lightly.
Asui haggles with a vendor, flamboyant.
Asui carries a bamboo basket through the market crowd.
Asui pauses at the market mouth and looks back toward the orchard.
By the rootstock bed, Aya and Asui stand side by side—one indigo headscarf, one cream scarf.
Aya hands a scion to Asui; they check bud eyes together.
Asui smooths Aya's indigo headscarf; they walk slowly along the berm.
Aya and Asui part at the bed end—one to the shed, one to the market.
Evening wind passes; their similar yellow vests cross among green seedlings and separate.
Months later at night, Qiao Bai alone sorts tomorrow's scions in the nursery shed.

Qiao Bai opens the phenology notebook（The same phenology notebook soaked through by muddy water, cover wrinkled, writing bled） and finds storm mud water has already soaked and wrinkled the oilcloth cover.
Qiao Bai wipes mud flecks from the grafting-knife handle.
Qiao Bai looks toward the pitch-dark rootstock bed.
The grafting knife glints cold under the lamp; Qiao Bai slowly sheaths it.
Qiao Bai slips blotting paper into the stained pages and presses them under the scion weight stone.
In rainy season, Qiao Bai hangs damp ties to dry in the nursery shed.
Qiao Bai brushes resin from the grafting-knife sheath with a bristle brush.
At dawn, Qiao Bai checks bamboo-tag dates in the rootstock bed.
Qiao Bai hangs a raincoat on a shed post and listens to turtledoves.
In high summer, Qiao Bai shades the rootstock bed with sun netting.
Qiao Bai checks wax-seal softness so it will not turn brittle.
When autumn wind rises, Qiao Bai closes the scion cold-box lid by the berm.
On a blank phenology-book page Qiao Bai tries new stock-scion combo codes.
On a frost night, Qiao Bai lights a barn lantern and checks flashlight charge.
Qiao Bai wraps the scion bundles in a blanket against night freeze.
On a heavy-snow day, Qiao Bai sweeps thin snow from the old garden porch stone steps.
Qiao Bai warms hands with breath and tightens a tie.
In early spring, Qiao Bai trims wild roses by the porch.
Qiao Bai re-traces writing on the five bamboo tags.
Qiao Bai posts a new grafting schedule on the shed wall.
Around the Dragon Boat Festival, Qiao Bai smokes the cold box with mugwort against insects.
Qiao Bai rewets the scion hemp cloth.
Qiao Bai alone paces the rootstock bed, silently recalling the bud-graft mnemonic.
After rain, Qiao Bai pushes open the shed door and listens to eave water drip into the jar.
Qiao Bai swaps worn gloves for new ones.
Another dusk, Qiao Bai sits by the grafting knife listening to insects.
At night Qiao Bai rises and patches mud on the berm.
Qiao Bai stores newly arrived ties by color.
Qiao Bai wipes the Bai Garden plaque on the porch.
Qiao Bai checks orchard-tractor oil level.
Against a drawing Qiao Bai marks dense planting row spacing.
Qiao Bai wrings a mud-stained rag dry and hangs it.
On a full-moon night, Qiao Bai looks from the bed at seedlings; dew beads silver.
Qiao Bai tidies the berm so bamboo tags all face the same way.
Inside the cover Qiao Bai writes the new season's budbreak notes.
Qiao Bai polishes the two wind chimes.
Hearing market cart-and-horse sounds, Qiao Bai keeps cutting scions.
Qiao Bai glues a cracked bamboo basket.
In a shed corner Qiao Bai stacks rootstock seedlings ready for use.
Qiao Bai seals the cold box tight against night temperature swings.
Another Qingming, Qiao Bai sets a bunch of wildflowers on the porch.
Qiao Bai rolls drawings into a tube and binds them with a rubber band.
Qiao Bai tries a light wind-chime ring; the tone is crisp.
Qiao Bai sits silent in the shed, listening long to water dripping from leaf tips.
Qiao Bai cuts worn indigo cloth into rag stock.
Qiao Bai clears cut waste twigs from the bed ditch.
At dawn, Qiao Bai patrols the rootstock bed; the orchard tractor waits at the head.
Qiao Bai crouches to check mud depth on the tractor tires.
Qiao Bai walks to the shed shade; those earlier three Fuji scion bundles still wrap in wet hemp cloth.
A green spray cart（A green spray cart, long thin body, no Bai Garden lettering—unlike the red tractor） rolls along the berm—long thin body, not the Bai Garden tractor.
Standing in the rootstock bed, Qiao Bai rechecks by bamboo-tag numbers whether unions are pushing new buds.
Qiao Bai hangs a wet raincoat on the berm wood rack.
Qiao Bai brushes mud flecks from the sleeve and glances back at the shed lamp.
After Grain Rain, Qiao Bai teaches a new apprentice to read bud-eye orientation in the rootstock bed.
Qiao Bai refolds sun-dried raincoats into the tractor toolbox.
In summer heat, Qiao Bai lays a wet cloth on the scion hemp wrap to keep moisture.
Qiao Bai checks the tractor rear bed and moves damp seedling bags to the upper tier.
On an autumn night, under a barn lantern, Qiao Bai rethreads mud-stained phenology loose pages.
Qiao Bai rotates updates among the five bamboo tags.
At first snow, Qiao Bai sweeps a narrow path across the porch threshold.
Qiao Bai reoils the practice folding knife and boxes it.
Hearing wind chimes ring lightly, Qiao Bai keeps revising the schedule.
Qiao Bai pushes open the shed door so a draft can carry damp away.
Qiao Bai hangs rain canvas on the porch.
Qiao Bai stores chipped old blades in an iron box.
At night Qiao Bai dreams of a survival-rate crash and, waking, writes bed numbers on a small blackboard.
Qiao Bai rinses bamboo tags with clear water.
Qiao Bai wipes the grafting schedule clean and reposts it.
Qiao Bai pulls weeds from berm stone seams.
Qiao Bai resticks bamboo tags in the berm; writing has faded some.
Before putting out the lamp, Qiao Bai glances once more at the grafting-knife edge.
Qiao Bai folds an indigo headscarf an apprentice left in the shed.
Hearing the market's closing horn, Qiao Bai rises and locks up.
By the charcoal fire Qiao Bai dries gloves.
Qiao Bai moves the wind chimes aside to show the just-repaired eaves.
Qiao Bai air-dries humidity test strips.
On the last phenology-book page Qiao Bai draws a survival-rate comparison.
Silently recalling tomorrow's bed numbers to graft, Qiao Bai steps out of the porch.
Qiao Bai drives the tractor to the wall foot, clearing scion-cutting floor space.
Hearing distant cockcrow, Qiao Bai blows out the barn lantern.
Another rainy night, Qiao Bai alone keeps watch over the scions until dawn.
Qiao Bai cuts newly arrived wax-seal blocks into small cubes.
Qiao Bai writes guest-ordered varieties on the small blackboard.
A storm breaks; the slope turns to mud; wind howls like a nursery alarm.
Lightning lights the shed; the tool bench rocks hard.
A crisp crack—the grafting knife（The same grafting knife with a chipped blade, rough cut edge, wood handle thick with resin） blade chips; the cut edge goes rough.
On the head-of-bed slope, the red orchard tractor skids and tips.
The orchard tractor（After rolling on a slope, the orchard tractor has a twisted bed and broken front wheel—a wreck） rolls over; bed twisted, front wheel broken—utterly wrecked.
Qiao Bai lunges at the tool bench and clutches the chipped grafting knife.
Neighbors arrive with lamps; the bed head is a mud slurry.
Next day, Qiao Bai stands in the nursery shed staring at the chipped grafting knife.
Qiao Bai brushes the blade notch with a finger, face dark.
On a blank place in the phenology book Qiao Bai sketches the broken front wheel and notes the date the orchard tractor rolled.
On the wall still hangs a photo of the orchard tractor loaded with rootstock seedlings; Qiao Bai cleans the frame.
Qiao Bai takes one of the five bamboo tags from the berm and rewrites the date.
The chipped grafting knife still rests on the bench; the blade notch is clear.
Qiao Bai sets muddy boots at the door to drain.
Weeks later, Qiao Bai brings in a knife grinder and sets the chipped edge beside a wet whetstone.

From a case Qiao Bai takes out a practice folding knife（A practice folding knife with a shorter blade and no Bai mark, much like the grafting knife but unfit for bud grafting） for comparison—shorter, no Bai mark, unable to cut a bud-graft bevel.
The grinder pushes the whetstone finely along the notch; a water line runs down the edge.

After the notch is ground flat and finished on a fine oilstone, the grafting knife（After rehoning the grafting knife blade is sharp again; the Bai on the handle remains, fine grind marks left） blade is sharp again; the Bai on the handle remains.
The repaired grafting knife cuts rootstock into a smooth tongue cut; Qiao Bai nods with relief.
Qiao Bai resets a bud shield, presses wax seal on the union, and wraps the tie tight.

At the bed head comes nursery merchant Lao Tian（Nursery merchant Lao Tian, full beard and bamboo basket on the back, build like Qiao Bai's but sturdier） with a bamboo basket of rootstock seedlings, build like Qiao Bai's but no straw hat.
The agronomy supervisor（A lean agronomy supervisor in a white coat with a chest badge, build like Qiao Bai's but more rigid） also arrives, white-coat badge damp with dew, talking beside Qiao Bai.
The supervisor points at the green spray cart's long thin tank, asking whether it belongs with the Bai Garden tractor.
The supervisor leaves; Qiao Bai alone remains in the rootstock bed.
Lao Tian unloads a bundle of rootstock seedlings, bows, and departs.

To the market comes girl Xiaoli（Market girl Xiaoli in a light-brown headscarf; at a glance like young Aya, shy unfamiliar eyes） in a light-brown headscarf; at a glance she somewhat resembles young Aya.
Xiaoli practices stacking apple baskets by fruit diameter; Qiao Bai shakes his head—her light-brown scarf is not Aya's indigo headscarf.
Xiaoli shyly bows her head and tightens the scarf.

Years later at dusk, Qiao Bai（The same Qiao Bai: rubber boots cracked, knee bandaged, walking slowly with a peach-wood cane, straw hat still on） with a bandaged knee leans on a cane at the old garden porch（Old garden porch: gray-tile porch; mottled Bai Garden plaque on the lintel; moss on the stone steps）.
Qiao Bai looks up at the Bai Garden plaque, gaze far away.
Those two wind chimes from under the shed eaves are moved to the porch for a trial ring; Qiao Bai stops to listen.
Qiao Bai sets a palm on the porch's cold stone pillar, as if saying goodbye.
Evening wind lifts the edge of his cracked rubber boot.
By day, adult Aya（Aya in the twenties, still the indigo headscarf, upright and steady） returns along the dirt road and hurries toward the old garden porch.
Under the porch Aya reunites with cane-leaning Qiao Bai; they embrace.
Beside the inner cot, Aya holds Qiao Bai's hand.

Qiao Bai（Qiao Bai has left the post; only his green rubber boots and straw hat remain in the nursery—he himself no longer appears）'s breath fades; he finally closes his eyes and steps away from the post.
Aya sets Qiao Bai's straw hat by the pillow.
Behind the shed door Qiao Bai's green rubber boots still hang; Aya reaches to stroke them gently.
On the porch pillar, Aya stands before a newly nailed memorial wood plaque（A cypress memorial plaque nailed to the porch pillar, carved with Qiao Bai's name and founding year）.
Aya's fingertip traces Qiao Bai's name carved on the plaque.
Aya sets a bunch of wildflowers under the plaque.
Remade-face Asui（After remaking the look, Asui still wears the cream silk scarf, expression deeper） arrives from the market and tightly embraces Aya under the porch.
Aya and Asui stand side by side on the porch—one quiet-eyed, one deep-faced.
They look at each other in silence, at faces alike.
Asui tightens the cream silk scarf; Aya still wears the indigo headscarf.
The shot returns to years ago—that youth practicing wrapping ties in the rootstock bed appears again.
Opening lamp light returns to the shed; a short-handled sharp blade carved Bai glints as it first tests the edge.
Flashback to the market that year—the yellow-vest figure in a cream silk scarf flashes past.
That row of five variety little tags stands again in the wet berm soil.
Back to that seedling bed of first meeting; green seedlings neat as before.
Those two little bells under the shed eaves chime lightly again in the evening wind.
Aya tucks that mud-stained phenology book under an arm and walks into the nursery shed.
In the shade, those earlier three Fuji scion bundles still wrap in wet hemp cloth, bud eyes up.
Aya takes over the rehoned grafting knife and begins bud-grafting along rootstock cuts again.
New green sprouts from porch stone seams, like just-living bud points.
Aya ties the indigo headscarf tight; nursery-shed lamps light again.
